texts.preamble: M/S Three'S Foods Pvt. Ltd vs Food Safety Officer on 24 February, 2020 In The Court Of Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma District & Sessions Judge / Appellate Tribunal, Phc, New Delhi In the matter of: Fsat No. 17/2016 1. M/s Three's Foods Pvt. Ltd. 14/869, Mandoli Extension Delhi-110 093 2. M/s Holyland Marketing (P) Ltd. D-154, New Rajinder Nagar New Delhi-110 060 3. M/s Bercos Restaurant (Bercos Melody House) G-2/43, Middle Circle Connaught Place New Delhi-110 001 .....Appellants Versus Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Gnct of Delhi 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan Connaught Place New Delhi-110 001 ..... Respondent Date of filing of appeal : 17.03.2015 Date of arguments : 19.02.2020 Date of judgment : 24.02.2020 Fsat No. 17/2016 Page No. 1 of 10 Judgment
texts.facts: 1. The appellants have filed the present appeal challenging the impugned order dated 10.12.2014 vide which the Adjudicating Officer imposed a penalty of Rs.2,00,000/-, Rs.2,00,000 and Rs.1,00,000/- upon Appellant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 respectively. 2. The facts in brief are that the Food Safety Officer (in short 'FSO') (took a sample of 'White Vinegar (Non Fruit), the food article on 24.12.2013 under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'the FSS Act, 2006) for analysis from M/s Bercos Restaurant. The sampled food commodity was analyzed by the Food Analyst who reported the sample in question as sub- standard because the M/S Three'S Foods Pvt. Ltd vs Food Safety Officer on 24 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156933222/ 1 acidity was found to be less than the prescribed minimum limit of 3.75%. The sample of food article was manufactured by M/s Three's Foods Pvt. Ltd. having its registered office at Mandoli Extension, Delhi-110 093. The manufacturer sold the food article to its distributor M/s Holyland Marketing (P) Ltd. vide Bill No. 275 dated 04.12.2013. The distributor sold the food article to M/s Bercos Restaurant, Connaught Place, New Delhi through the company M/s Deling and Company with which it was having contract for making purchases and cooking the food for its restaurant vide Bill No. T1-2091/13-14 dated 11.12.2013. 3. The FSO filed complaint before the Adjudicating Officer, New Delhi against the the appellants i.e. manufacturer, distributor and M/s Bercos Restaurant for the offence u/s 26/51 and 52 of the FSS Act, 2006. During proceedings before the Adjudicating Officer, M/s Three's Foods Pvt. Ltd. admitted to have manufactured the food article in question and also admitted to have supplied the same to M/s Holyland Marketing (P) Ltd. It was also not disputed that M/s Holyland Marketing (P) Ltd. had supplied the food article to M/s Bercos Restaurant. The bills to these effect are also on record. 5. Aggrieved by the order of Adjudicating Officer, the appellants have filed the present appeal challenging the impugned order on the following grounds: i) The Food Analyst vide Report No. FSS/1387/2013 dated 06.01.2014 specifically mentioned that the sample meets with the requirement of Regulation No. 2.2 of the FSS (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011. ii) The Food Analyst in his report only found the food article to be sub-standard and despite this, the Adjudicating Officer wrongly relied upon the FSO and held the appellants guilty for misbrand also. iii) The findings by the Food Analyst on note sheet dated 22.05.2014 mention that the address of packaging company is Sec. A-3, Tronika City, Loni, Ghaziabad but the name of the manufacturer is not declared on the label and the same is declared by the official as partial violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2.6(i) of the FSS (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 and the same could not have been taken into account, as the same was issued beyond fourteen days of the receipt of the sample. Therefore, it is indicative of the fact that counterparts of the sample were not identical as required to be lifted by the FSO as per Rule 2.4.1.15 of the FSS Rules, 2011. iv) The Food Analyst Report dated 06.01.2014 sent to the manufacturer and distributor u/s 46(4) of the FSS Act, 2006 only disclosed that the sample was found to be sub-standard and not misbranded and, therefore, the appellants could not have been punished for the misbranding. v) The Adjudicating Officer during inquiry ignored the fact of admission by the manufacturer for having sold the food in question to the distributor in the same condition by valid bill, which in turn sold the food article in question to M/s Bercos Restaurant in the same condition. Therefore, the M/S Three'S Foods Pvt. Ltd vs Food Safety Officer on 24 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156933222/ 2 Adjudicating Officer ignored the defence of due diligence available to the appellants with respect to guarantee u/s 26(4) of the FSS Act, 2006 read with Section 80(2) (D) (E) of the FSS Act, 2006. vi) The Adjudicating Officer ignored the fact that even as per the report of Food Analyst, there was marginal deficiency of acetic acid which can occur on account of human error while analyzing the sample and, therefore, such high penalty could not have been imposed. 6. Along with the appeal, an application for condonation of delay has also been filed. In view of the averments made in the application, the delay is condoned. 7. Ld.
texts.arguments: Counsel for the appellants submits that the Adjudicating Officer has passed the order mechanically as he has not taken into account the fact that the manufacturer had admitted to have sold the food article in question to the distributor who sold the same to M/s Bercos Restaurant in same condition vide valid bill. He further submits that the guarantee of defence could have been extended to them. He further submits that as per the report of Food Analyst, the labelling requirement under the FSS Rules, 2011 was in order and, therefore, the appellants could not have been punished for the misbrand. 8. Per contra, Ld. Sr. PP for the State/respondent submits that the Adjudicating Officer has duly appreciated the facts and rightly punished the appellants. He further submits that for the offence u/s 52 of the FSS Act, 2006, the manufacturer, packer and FBO are equally liable. The provisions have been made to protect the consumers. He further submits that the object of such declaration is that in the event of article being found spurious, the same can immediately be taken charge from the address of the packers and manufacturers. Section 51 of the FSS Act, 2006 provides penalty for sub- standard food, which reads as under: "Penalty for sub-standard food. - Any person who whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption which is sub-standard, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to five lakh rupees." 15. Bare perusal of this Section provides penalty of rupees five lakh for manufacturing for sale or storing or selling or distributing or importing any article of food for human consumption which is sub-standard. Section 80 (B) of the said Act provides defence of due diligence. Section 80(B)(2)(d) and (e) of the said Act provide as under: "(d) In the case of an offence involving the sale of food, that (i) the person sold the food in the same condition as and when the person purchased it, or (ii) the person sold the food in a different condition to that in which the person purchased it, but that the difference did not result in any contravention of this Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder, and (e) that the person did not know and had no reason to suspect at the time of commission of the alleged offence that the person's act or omission would constitute an offence under the relevant section.
